test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 25 May 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: ‘Waiting for a Visa’ is an autobiographical work of which of the following leaders of India?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Waiting for a Visa is a 20-page autobiographical life story of **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar written **in the period 1935–36.
 
• It consists of reminiscences drawn by Ambedkar, related to his experiences with untouchability, in his own handwriting.
 
• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar written (14 April 1891 – 6 December 1956) was an Indian jurist, economist, social reformer, and political leader who headed the committee drafting the Constitution of India from the Constituent Assembly debates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Why I Am an Atheist is an essay written by Indian revolutionary Bhagat Singh in 1930 in Lahore Central Jail. 
 
• The essay was a reply to his religious friends who thought Bhagat Singh became an atheist because of his vanity.
 
• Memoirs of My Life and Time in The Days of My Youth (1857-1864) was the autobiography of Bipin Chandra Pal. 
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai was an Indian author, freedom fighter, and politician. He played a vital role in the Indian Independence movement. He was popularly known as Punjab Kesari.
 
• He was one of the three members of the Lal Bal Pal Trimurti.
